Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that these studies suggest a potential role for AMPK (adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase) in modulating melatonin secretion. The effect of metformin or AICAR (a compound known to activate AMPK) on melatonin plasma concentrations in ewes may indicate that AMPK plays a crucial role in the regulation of this hormone.

In other words, these studies suggest that injecting metformin or AICAR into an intracerebroventricularly administered dose may help modulate the levels of melatonin. This implies that AMPK is involved in regulating the secretion of melatonin and highlights the potential significance of AMPK activation as a metabolic cue for modulating this hormone.

These studies support the idea that AMPK acts on both the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) and/or directly within the pineal gland to influence melatonin secretion, suggesting that it is a key player in regulating melatonin levels. Overall, these findings suggest a potential relationship between AMPK activation and melatonin secretion.
